correctness.rationale: The finite distributive max-min walk identity reduces each iterated possibility grade to a rooted path bottleneck. For a fixed depth k, (n-1)_k rooted simple paths each have threshold probability (x_k n^{-k/(k+1)})^{k+1}, yielding limiting Poisson mean x_k^{k+1}. Distinct path pairs sharing h primitive variables have at least h common nonroot vertices; overlap-template counting bounds the dependency contribution O(n^{-1/(K+1)}). The exact thresholds for shared variables and dependency-graph Chen–Stein theorem yield a joint Poisson zero-event bound. Repeated-vertex walks with m<k distinct nonroot vertices have at least m independent edge grades plus an independent endpoint mark; their contribution is O(n^{(m-k)/(k+1)}). This gives joint Weibull upper-orthant limits with independent components. A finite standalone checker verifies walk identities and pair-overlap templates; finite checks alone are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected full Gödel witnessed-model semantics and theorems of Ferrari et al. (2026); they study calculi, finite-model theory and complexity rather than iid random fuzzy frames. Eliazar, Metzler and Reuveni (2019) study row/column extremes of independent-entry random matrices, not iterative graph-path max-min composition with a common terminal valuation. The Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon (1989) bound is a tool, not the claim. Targeted published-record semantic searches found a finite-frame ordinal-regrading classification but no asserted joint Weibull law. Specialized probabilistic priority remains a nonzero risk.
residual_risks: The specialist literature on random max-min matrix powers and random rooted path bottlenecks was not exhaustively inspected and may contain an equivalent result.
